subject: A taskq record quoted in a document must not become a task
description:
The result-side decode runs on EVERY tool result, not just a shell one, because a
tool_result carries only a tool_use_id and no tool name. So a session that READS a file
containing an example record picks it up as a real mutation.

Measured 2026-08-31: taskq-DESIGN.md section 9 prints a sample record verbatim
(op=claim, task=12, subject="Activity pane: humanize ETA"). Two unrelated sessions that had
read that doc both show a phantom task #12 in the panel. Reading this repos own
claude-replay-engine/src/engine/taskq.rs test fixtures does the same, and produced a
further eight subject-less stubs in the session that wrote them.

The v21 change that lets a create record stand its task up on its own makes these MORE
visible, which is the right trade for real tasks but sharpens this one.

Fix: gate the result-side decode on provenance -- only decode records from the result of a
shell call whose command actually invoked the taskq program. The call side already applies
that test (taskq_calls requires the word before the verb to be the program); the result
side cannot today because it has no access to the call.

That needs the adapter to carry a little state: remember the tool_use_ids of shell calls
whose command mentioned taskq, and decode a result only for those. Claude decode_line
already threads a &mut String cwd, so it has somewhere to put it; Codex has a
LinePreprocessor with real state. Both would need the set.

Cheaper partial: a record inside a Read result is far more suspicious than one in a Bash
result, but the tool name is not available at the result either, so this is the same
problem wearing a smaller hat.

Definition of done: reading taskq-DESIGN.md in a session creates no tasks; a session that
actually runs taskq is unchanged; a fixture covering both.
activeForm: Gating taskq records on call provenance
